narrative: The model estimated a 93.0% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In this admissions process, that high predicted risk led directly to rejection of your law school application, because the school uses expected bar-passage likelihood as a key condition for admission. The decision was not based on gender or race. All three top factors pointed in the same direction, producing a very high failure-risk estimate. To proceed, ask admissions for a formal review or appeal, explain any extenuating circumstances behind your class ranks or LSAT, and ask whether a retake, additional coursework, or a structured bar-preparation plan could support a future application. Meet with an academic advisor to build a remediation plan before reapplying.
